slides.title: Infra or product: who are you hiring?
options: Product: turns it into something people use
slides.sub: Both are Web3 engineers. They are not the same hire. Swipe for the difference.

slides.title: The layer it all runs on.
rows: Getting data on and off chain, fast
slides.sub: Often Rust, Go or C++. Thinks in systems and failure modes.

slides.title: Builds what users touch.
rows: Wiring the frontend to on-chain logic
slides.sub: Often TypeScript and React, sometimes Solidity. Thinks in users and outcomes.

slides.title: Ask what is actually breaking.
slides.sub: Downtime, slow calls, data you can't trust: that's an infrastructure problem. Users dropping off, features stuck in the backlog: that's a product problem.

slides.title: One job spec for both.
slides.sub: A protocol engineer screened on React questions. A frontend lead grilled on consensus theory. Write the spec around the problem, not the buzzwords, and the right people apply.

slides.title: Not sure which you need?
slides.sub: We help Web3, crypto and AI teams scope the role before the search starts. Send us your brief and we'll talk it through.
